answer: A deposit-backed identity registry resists Sybil attacks the way a cedar grove resists a storm: each agent must lock a meaningful stake to register, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. The registry acts as a mirror - every agent stake, history and attestation is publicly visible, so a newcomer with no record earns no trust until it has completed real work. If an agent misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its voyage through the economy ends; honest agents keep their deposits and build reputation over time, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
